newsitem.title: USA: N.J. puts off vote on $2.9 bln pension bond deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. puts off vote on $2.9 bln pension bond deal.

text.p: The New Jersey Assembly late Monday put off a vote on a plan to borrow $2.9 billion of pension obligation bonds, possibly delaying the decision until May.

Assembly Speaker Jack Collins, a Salem County Republican, said he would not post the bill for a vote until after the Senate acts. That could delay the plan until May, since April is booked for budget hearings and negotiations.

Democrats quoting skeptical Wall Street credit monitors raised a storm of protest. Republican Assembly members did not want to take a controversial vote if the bill was going to be voted down in the state Senate, where several key Republicans have questioned the plan.

The plan would have enabled Gov. Christie Whitman to have balanced her budget by avoiding $647 million in state payments to the pension funds. The bond issue would have been used to fully fund the state's public employees pension system.
